tasks.title: Task 1: Create an Eventstream Source
tasks.objective: Create a Fabric Eventstream that uses Azure Event Hubs as its data source and open it to preview incoming data.
tasks.expectedOutcome: An Eventstream named es_Fabrikam_InternetSales is connected to the Azure Event Hub source, becomes Active, and shows sample data in the preview window.

facts.fact: The source type selected for the stream is Azure Event Hubs.
facts.quote: for this class we will select the option **Azure Event Hubs**.

facts.fact: A new connection is created for the Azure Event Hub source.
facts.quote: Click on the **New connection** text since you do not currently have a connection.

facts.fact: The Event Hub namespace is set to rtiadhub<inject key="DeploymentID" enableCopy="false"/>.
facts.quote: rtiadhub<inject key="DeploymentID" enableCopy="false"/>

facts.fact: The Event Hub is set to rti-iad-orders.
facts.quote: rti-iad-orders

facts.fact: The Shared Access Key Name is set to rti-reader.
facts.quote: rti-reader

facts.fact: The Skip Test Connection box is unchecked.
facts.quote: Uncheck the **Skip Test Connection** box.

facts.fact: The Eventstream is renamed to es_Fabrikam_InternetSales.
facts.quote: let’s call our Eventstream **es_Fabrikam_InternetSales**.

facts.fact: After creation, the Eventstream source should become Active and show sample data in preview.
facts.quote: It may take a few moments for your Source to be **Active**

tasks.title: Task 2: Setup Eventstream Transformations
tasks.objective: Set up two parallel filter transformations in the Eventstream and route their outputs to separate Eventhouse KQL tables for rapid and standard deliveries.
tasks.expectedOutcome: The Eventstream contains a RapidDelivery filter for IsRapidDelivery = 1 and a StandardDelivery filter for IsRapidDelivery = 0, each connected to an Eventhouse destination writing to the corresponding KQL table.

facts.fact: A filter transformation is created with Name set to RapidDelivery.
facts.quote: Name: **RapidDelivery**

facts.fact: The RapidDelivery filter uses the field IsRapidDelivery and keeps events where the value equals 1.
facts.quote: Field: **IsRapidDelivery**

facts.fact: The RapidDelivery filter keeps events when the value equals 1.
facts.quote: Equals: **1**

facts.fact: The RapidDelivery Eventhouse destination is named eh-RapidDelivery.
facts.quote: Destination name: **eh-RapidDelivery**

facts.fact: The RapidDelivery destination writes to a KQL table named RapidDelivery.
facts.quote: TableName: **RapidDelivery**

facts.fact: A second filter transformation is created with Name set to StandardDelivery.
facts.quote: Name: **StandardDelivery**

facts.fact: The StandardDelivery filter keeps events when the value equals 0.
facts.quote: Equals: **0**

facts.fact: The StandardDelivery destination writes to a KQL table named StandardDelivery.
facts.quote: TableName: **StandardDelivery**

tasks.title: Task 3: Exploring the KQL Database
tasks.objective: Explore the eh_Fabrikam KQL Database in the RTI_ODL_User<inject key="DeploymentID" enableCopy="false"></inject> workspace, refresh its metrics, and inspect the RapidDelivery table overview and details.
tasks.expectedOutcome: The learner has opened the eh_Fabrikam KQL Database, refreshed and reviewed its database information, and viewed the RapidDelivery table overview showing metadata and streaming data details.

facts.fact: The workspace to return to is named RTI_ODL_User<inject key="DeploymentID" enableCopy="false"></inject>.
facts.quote: Make your way back to your workspace: **RTI_ODL_User<inject key="DeploymentID" enableCopy="false"></inject>**.

facts.fact: The KQL Database item to open is eh_Fabrikam.
facts.quote: Open the **eh_Fabrikam** KQL Database item.

facts.fact: The learner must click the refresh icon in the top-left corner of the screen.
facts.quote: Click on the **refresh icon** in the top-left corner of the screen as well there are other items to view:

facts.fact: The database size should continue to grow over time.
facts.quote: The size of the database should continue to grow.

facts.fact: The table to select in the KQL Database is named RapidDelivery.
facts.quote: click on the table within your KQL Database called **RapidDelivery.**

facts.fact: The Data Preview section shows a preview of table ingestion results.
facts.quote: **Data Preview** – Shows a preview of the table ingestion results.

facts.fact: The Table Details section shows compressed and original size, OneLake availability, and number of rows.
facts.quote: **Table Details** – Shows Compressed and Original size of table, OneLake availability, number of rows in the tables and various other details.

tasks.title: Task 4: Learning to write KQL
tasks.objective: Learn the basics of writing and running KQL queries against the KQL Database by replacing template table names with RapidDelivery and using operators like take, count, project, project-away, and union.
tasks.expectedOutcome: The learner successfully runs KQL queries on the RapidDelivery table and sees returned rows, record counts, and projected results in the default KQL Queryset.

facts.fact: The learner should use the ribbon option named Query with code.
facts.quote: Query with code.

facts.fact: On Line 8, YOUR_TABLE_HERE should be replaced with RapidDelivery.
facts.quote: replace that with the table name, **RapidDelivery**.

facts.fact: The learner should highlight Line 8 and 9 and click Run.
facts.quote: Highlight **Line 8 and 9** and click on the **Run** button in the top-left corner of the window

facts.fact: The example query returns 100 rows.
facts.quote: For this example, 100 rows will be returned.

facts.fact: On Line 12, YOUR_TABLE_HERE should be replaced with RapidDelivery.
facts.quote: replace that with the table name, **RapidDelivery**.

facts.fact: A sample query projects specific columns from RapidDelivery after taking 5 rows.
facts.quote: | project CustomerKey, OrderDate, ProductKey, UnitPrice, OrderQuantity

facts.fact: The project-away example excludes EventEnqueuedUtcTime, EventProcessedUtcTime, and PartitionId.
facts.quote: | project-away EventEnqueuedUtcTime, EventProcessedUtcTime, PartitionId

facts.fact: The KQL Database currently contains two tables named RapidDelivery and StandardDelivery.
facts.quote: You currently have two tables in your KQL Database, RapidDelivery and StandardDelivery.

tasks.title: Task 5: Using T-SQL Queries Against a KQL Database
tasks.objective: Use the KQL Queryset to translate a T-SQL aggregation query into KQL with explain, then run both the translated KQL and the original SQL against the KQL database.
tasks.expectedOutcome: A query tab shows the SQL-to-KQL translation for the product quantity aggregation, and executing both the pasted KQL query and the original SQL query returns the expected results.

facts.fact: Open a new tab in the default queryset by clicking the plus symbol.
facts.quote: In the top menu, click on the **+** symbol to open a new tab.

facts.fact: Begin the new query with the explain directive prefixed by comment markers.
facts.quote: Within the new query window, start the new query with **-- explain**.

facts.fact: Use the provided SQL aggregation query on RapidDelivery grouped by ProductKey.
facts.quote:
SELECT 
    ProductKey, SUM(OrderQuantity) AS TotalQuantity From RapidDelivery
GROUP BY
    ProductKey

facts.fact: Run the full selection including the explain lines.
facts.quote: Select the entire query, including the -- explain and click Run.

facts.fact: The explain output initially appears as a single record.
facts.quote: The output will be a single record.

facts.fact: Copy the translated KQL from the output and run it in the query pane.
facts.quote: Copy the translated query from the output seen in the previous screenshot. Paste the query in your query pane. Highlight and run the query to retrieve the results.

facts.fact: Run only the original SQL statement as an alternative query method.
facts.quote: Highlight the original SQL statement that was used to translate the KQL query and run only that.
